Caliper & Crayon Type Directions
Caliper & Crayon · type directions · for reviewSame Archie content three times. Only the type and its spacing change.

Three directions, all available on Google Fonts so they load anywhere. Each keeps the caliper/crayon idea in the type itself rather than the color: a precise, measured system with one expressive register.

My pick is A. It has the most character at display size and reads cleanly at text size from the same family, and the mono for metadata gives the role block a measured, instrument-panel feel without a second font family to manage.

ABricolage Grotesque + DM MonoBricolage has an optical-size axis: tight, slightly quirky at headline size, plain and even at text size. DM Mono for roles, dates and labels. Two families, both variable.

Archie: Gold in the Fire

A memoir I edited, designed and published for a man I never met.

Role
Editing, book design, publishing
Author
Archie I. Floyd, Jr.
Year
2019
Place
Oakland, California
Format
Paperback, 6 × 9 in
PDF, 8 MB

In his "rigorously honest" memoir, Archie Floyd recounts his troubled childhood, addiction to crack cocaine, and the criminal consequences of repeated car theft, and critiques the Ohio criminal justice system from the perspective of a Black man.

What I did

I edited the manuscript for structure and clarity while keeping Archie's voice, designed the interior and cover, set the type, and handled printing and the Amazon listing myself. How I came to publish the memoir of a man I never met is in the foreword.

BArchivo, one family, width axisHeadlines set expanded, labels set condensed, text set normal. The width axis is the whole system, which is a quietly literal caliper idea, and it keeps a condensed nod to the current wordmark.

Shared changes across all three, from the review: title keeps its real capitalization; book pages sit on a tinted plinth with a shadow so the cover has an edge; the role column gets a top rule and a mono or condensed label register so it holds its own against the title; the summary moves up beside the title so the header fills the width. The "6 × 9 in" format line is a placeholder until SJ confirms the trim size.
